stem.text: An L-shape is made from a rectangle 12 cm by 8 cm. A corner 4 cm by 7 cm is cut out. What is the area of the L-shape?

options.execution: The child finds the area of the whole 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle, 96 cm², and forgets to take away the 4 cm by 7 cm cut-out. Taking away 28 cm² gives 68 cm².
The child adds the sides of the 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle, 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40, when asked for area. The area is 12 × 8 − 4 × 7 = 96 − 28 = 68 cm².
The child works out 96 − 28 in columns and takes the smaller digit from the larger in the ones, 8 − 6 = 2. The tens give 9 − 2 = 7, so they write 72 cm² instead of 68 cm².
